source.title: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic Function: Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosage. Guidance for Industry
source.status: draft guidance (not for implementation; comments due 1 December 2026)
source.replaces: the May 2003 final guidance of the same name, when finalised
source.extraction: AI-assisted, 5 November 2026, from the text of the PDF at the URL above as returned by a web-fetch tool (the PDF itself is not in the repository or the owner's source folder). Quotes are as returned. Tables 1 and 2 came back as flattened text; their reading below is the assistant's and is marked as such. Not yet reviewed by the platform owner.

child_pugh.quote: FDA recommends using the Child-Pugh (CP) classification to categorize the degree of HI in subjects with cirrhosis

nci_in_cancer.quote: In subjects with cancer, sponsors can use the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Organ Dysfunction Working Group criteria

nci_not_in_non_cancer.quote: FDA does not recommend the use of the NCI Criteria to assess hepatic function for non-cancer patients.

cp_groups.quote: HI is classified as mild, moderate, or severe, which corresponds to CP scores of 5-6 (CP group A), 7-9 (CP group B), and 10-15 (CP group C), respectively.

nci_components.quote: The NCI Criteria uses total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase to assess HI

other_systems.quote: MELD scores can be useful for further stratification of disease severity within CP groups B and C.
